title: New Orleans bands: Celestin and Manuel Perez
summary: Allen and the interviewer discuss Celestin's and Manuel Perez's bands and that he met Piron only in New York.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Early 20s. Early 20s. I'd say about 24. I'm not, I'm not much unremembered big. Well they had a few big bands. I think Celestan had a big band by then. Yeah, they had seven pieces I think. Celestan, I've heard him record on the television,

the radio since I learned that. Celestan had a nice band since you mentioned it. I think he had seven, eight pieces. And then another guy that had trumpet playing, had a nice band. Yeah. Manuel Perez. Yeah. Manuel Perez. Man, that's the one. He's had a very nice band. I remember saying that when I was down, when I get old he was going over, I could continue to play, because at that time he must have been 40 or so. Was he that old then? I didn't know. Well that's what I think, because I remember saying he played so great, because he used to play opera on every Sunday. They used to run a high one of the local bands to play opera that's on a Sunday boat ride. And I heard he was going over and played so good, I used to sing, when I get old, you know, if I'd be able to play like him, but he'd still able to play. He was strong, was he? Yeah, strong, great. Very good trumpet playing. And his band was good too? And then we'll be like Celestine. What is Celestine? Celestine? Yeah, Celestine. Well he was on, he'd be on the books of silence too. They used local bands quite often for competition. How about Piran? Did you ever remember his band? No, I didn't remember his band. I met him in New York here I think.
